executive_summary: Forecast adherence was 38.5%, indicating a significant over‑forecast (actual contacts far below plan). The miss is already visible at the Channel level, so it is not unique to this queue; the primary driver is a lower‑than‑expected contact rate per warranty unit, while the number of units under warranty was essentially as planned. We are highly confident that the issue stems from the channel‑level forecast bias and recommend reviewing the contact‑rate assumptions in the Voice forecast plan.
business_impact: Over‑forecast leads to excess staffing and unnecessary labor costs for the Voice channel in ANZ Comm Client DSP Upsell.

ranked_root_causes.title: Miss inherited from Channel level
ranked_root_causes.explanation: The same over‑forecast is already present when looking at the Voice channel for the whole ANZ CSG business, so the queue‑specific forecast is not the root source.
ranked_root_causes.business_impact: Excess staffing allocated to the Voice channel across ANZ.
ranked_root_causes.recommended_action: Review and adjust the Voice channel forecast plan for the ANZ Comm Client DSP Upsell queue to align with observed contact rates.

ranked_root_causes.title: Lower contact rate per unit than planned
ranked_root_causes.explanation: The forecast assumed each warranty unit would generate more contacts than actually occurred; the planned ASU was close to actual, but the actual contacts per unit were far below plan, driving most of the miss.
ranked_root_causes.business_impact: Forecast overestimates needed staffing because it expects more calls per device than are realized.
ranked_root_causes.recommended_action: Revise the contact‑rate assumption (calls per warranty unit) in the forecasting model for this Voice queue, using recent actuals to recalibrate.
